items.title: データサイエンティストのための競馬入門(自分のノート)
items.content_html:
データサイエンティストのための競馬入門(自分のノート)

!!! Summary "Summary" 近年、競馬は単なるギャンブルではなく、データ分析を生かし、収益を狙うものとしてでも注目されています。 中央競馬（JRA）はレースや馬、騎手、血統などあらゆる情報がデジタル化されており、 データサイエンティストにとっては機械学習や統計モデルの実践フィールドとして非常に魅力的です。

本記事では、競馬の基本的な仕組みと、データ分析に必要な視点からの基礎知識を纏めて見ました。

items.title: Avoiding Overflow in Polars: What Every Python Developer Who Use Polars Should Know
items.content_html:
Avoiding Overflow in Polars: What Every Python Developer Who Use Polars Should Know

!!! Summary "Summary" When working with Polars, a lightning-fast DataFrame library built in Rust and designed for performance, many Python developers are surprised to encounter something they rarely see in standard Python: Overflow.

This post explains why overflow happens in Polars, how it differs from standard Python behaviour, and what you can do to prevent it.

items.title: cmp Command in Linux
items.content_html:
cmp Command in Linux

!!! summary "Summary" The cmp command in Linux is a powerful utility used to compare two files byte by byte. It is primarily used to identify differences between binary or text files, making it invaluable for tasks such as verifying file integrity or identifying modifications.

items.title: scp - Securely Copy Files
items.content_html:
scp - Securely Copy Files

!!! summary "Summary" The scp (Secure Copy) command is a command-line utility that allows you to securely copy files and directories between a local and a remote host, or between two remote hosts. It leverages the SSH protocol for secure data transfer.

items.title: umask Command in Linux
items.content_html:
umask Command in Linux

!!! summary "Summary" The umask command in Linux sets or displays the file mode creation mask, which determines the permissions of newly created files and directories. It's a crucial tool for controlling default permissions.

items.title: join Command in Linux
items.content_html:
join Command in Linux

!!! summary "Summary" The join command in Linux is used to combine lines from two files based on a common field. It's essentially a simplified database join operation performed on plain text files.

items.title: odt Command: Open Document Text (ODT) File Converter
items.content_html:
odt Command: Open Document Text (ODT) File Converter

!!! summary "Summary" The odt command, part of the odt2txt package, is a simple command-line utility for converting OpenDocument Text (.odt) files to plain text.

items.title: pushd Command in Linux
items.content_html:
pushd Command in Linux

!!! summary "Summary" The pushd command in Linux allows you to change the current directory and save the previous directory for easy return. It's part of the shell's directory stack management.

items.title: wc Command: Word, Line, and Byte Counting
items.content_html:
wc Command: Word, Line, and Byte Counting

!!! summary "Summary" The wc command in Linux is a versatile utility used for counting the number of lines, words, characters, and bytes within a file or input stream. It's a fundamental tool for text analysis and data manipulation.

items.title: wc - Word Count
items.content_html:
wc - Word Count

!!! summary "Summary" The wc command in Linux is a utility that displays the number of lines, words, and bytes (or characters) in a file. It's a simple yet powerful tool for quick text analysis.

items.title: Relearn Math as Adult A-Z(2): Functions
items.content_html: Demystify functions with this comprehensive guide designed for adult learners. Explore definitions, types, transformations, expansion, factorization, and plenty of examples to solidify your understanding.

items.title: dirname Command: Extracting Directory Names
items.content_html:
dirname Command: Extracting Directory Names

!!! summary "Summary" The dirname command extracts the directory portion of a given file name or path. It's useful for scripts where you need to work with the directory containing a file, rather than the file itself.

items.title: id Command: Display User and Group Information
items.content_html:
id Command: Display User and Group Information

!!! summary "Summary" The id command displays user and group information, including the user ID (UID), group ID (GID), and group memberships.

items.title: jobs Command: Managing Background Processes
items.content_html:
jobs Command: Managing Background Processes

!!! summary "Summary" The jobs command provides a convenient way to list, monitor, and manage background processes in your current shell environment. It is useful for checking the status of processes you've sent to the background using & or Ctrl+Z followed by bg.

items.title: ln Command: Creating Links in Linux
items.content_html:
ln Command: Creating Links in Linux

!!! summary "Summary" The ln command in Linux is used to create links between files. It allows you to access the same file through multiple names, either as hard links or symbolic (soft) links. This post will cover the usage of ln, provide examples, and explain the commonly used flags.

items.title: nohup Command in Linux
items.content_html:
nohup Command in Linux

!!! summary "Summary" The nohup command in Linux allows you to run a command that will continue to execute even after you close the terminal or log out. It prevents the command from receiving the SIGHUP (hang up) signal, which is typically sent when the terminal is closed.

items.title: nohup: Run Commands Unaffected by Disconnects
items.content_html:
nohup: Run Commands Unaffected by Disconnects

!!! summary "Summary" The nohup command allows you to run a command that will continue to execute even after you log out of the terminal or the terminal window is closed. It is particularly useful for long-running processes.

items.title: pushd and popd: Navigating Directories Like a Pro
items.content_html:
pushd and popd: Navigating Directories Like a Pro

!!! summary "Summary" pushd and popd are powerful commands for navigating directories in Linux, allowing you to quickly switch between directories and easily return to previous locations. Think of them as a stack for directories!

items.title: readlink Command in Linux
items.content_html:
readlink Command in Linux

!!! summary "Summary" The readlink command displays the target of a symbolic link. It's useful for determining the actual file or directory that a symbolic link points to.

items.title: rsync: Efficient File Synchronization and Transfer
items.content_html:
rsync: Efficient File Synchronization and Transfer

!!! summary "Summary" rsync is a versatile command-line utility for efficiently synchronizing files and directories between two locations, either locally or over a network. It minimizes data transfer by only copying the differences between the source and destination.
